recipes.name: Old-Fashioned Strawberry Pretzel Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) container frozen whipped topping, thawed

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Cream butter or margarine with the brown sugar. Mix in the pretzels and pat mixture into the bottom of one 9x13 inch baking pan. Bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 10 to 12 minutes. Set aside to cool.
In a medium bowl, dissolve the gelatin in the boiling water and stir in the strawberries. Chill until partially thickened.

In a small bowl beat the cream cheese and white sugar together until smooth. Fold in the whipped cream. Spread mixture over the top of the cooled crust, making sure to seal the edges. Chill then pour the gelatin mixture over he cream cheese layer. Chill until firm.

raw_recipe.headline: Old-Fashioned Strawberry Pretzel Salad
raw_recipe.description: A cool strawberry gelatin salad with a cream cheese middle and pretzel crust.

review.reviewBody:
My family has been making this salad for years and we've learned a few tricks I thought I would pass on. 
1) Freeze the pretzel layer until completely cooled and hardened.
2) Add 1/3 of a packet of gelatin to the jello mixture.
3) Allow the jello mixture to chill before pouring on top of the cream cheese layer.

Hope these hints help!

I followed the suggestions:
- spray non-stick cooking spray in pan
-completely cool crust (I made crust the night before...easy!)!
-1 1/2 times the creme cheese filling
-make sure cr. cheese filling touches all edges of pan
-added 1/3 pkg. gelatin to the jello and let it thicken some before putting it on top.

Then all you have to do is have extra copies of the recipe with you...to hand out! Everyone wants it

I'm all for fat and sugar when they're needed, but this light summer dessert (it's funny that it's called a salad) can be much less caloric with a few modifications that don't diminish the taste at all. First, one stick of butter (1/2 cup) is plenty, and you might not even need that much. You can use neufchatel in place of regular cream cheese, and you can cut the sugar in that neufchatel/cool whip layer to 1/2 cup or less. I also used sugar free jello. I followed everyone's tips about thoroughly cooling the crust, sealing the neufchatel layer to the edge of the dish, and not adding the jello/strawberry layer until almost set. It all worked wonderfully!

This really sounds great but when I got this recipe I simply used about 1 cup pecans and 
1 1/2 teaspoon sugar and a little (1 teaspoon)
butter mixed together as the bottom layer. Cooked it for 15 minutes at 350 degrees, let cool then added the other layers. Wow!

Here's a way to get some attention with this recipe: during the last minute of baking for the pretzel crust, sprinkle a 12 oz. bag of DARK chocolate chips on top of pretzel mixture. When you pull it out, spread the chocolate over the pretzels and make as directed. Your guests will be surprised at how the addition of chocolate makes this like a chocolate covered strawberry!

Made this for years its definitely a favorite and I love using fresh fruit I've also used frozen but fresh strawberries always taste amazing I've even added pecans to the pretzel crust and it was definitely delicious... i recently tried something new a lady I know gave me a tip to actually chill the jello till it's set then mix and spoon and spread it on top it eliminates the possibility of it leaking to the bottom and making your crust soggy... great recipe
love this recipe and for all of us lazy cooks out there you can make the crust and cream cheese layers by the recipe and just put pie filling on top I've used blueberry and it turned out great

This was soo good! I followed some of the suggestions and let the jello part set a little before I put it on. I also used French Vanilla Cool Whip which gave a little more flavor. Everyone loved this!

I think this is one of those recipes most people either love or hate. Hubs loved this and ate it within 48 hours. I thought it was just okay; however, my apathy could be because I used Splenda instead of normal sugar in the middle layer. I thought I'd humor hubs for once, and I didn't like the aftertaste. However, since he loved it so much I'm going to make it for him again; we have more Cool Whip and more pretzels. We do not have more strawberries, frozen or otherwise, so I'll try with the fruit we have (raspberries I think), and I'll just leave out the cream cheese since we don't have anymore. I didn't use the amount of cream cheese called for since 1. I didn't have it and 2. we've tried similar layers with cream cheese in jello salads and have not liked it at all. So, this is a variation for our house. I thought the instructions were easy, I froze each layer in between, started the jello first so it had time to cool, and did not have any seepage even though the strawberries created lumps (note: spoon in the jello layer, don't dump like I did!). Thanks for the recipe!

I made this recipe following all steps & I really liked the sweet & salty strawberry fresh flavor. But, if & when I make it again, I will be sure to make these 2 chages: first, I plan on crushing the pretzels more finely (the crust was too hard & crunchy), & second: I plan on slicing the strawberries. They're too big & lumpy when left whole or even when cut in half.

I have made this over and over. People always ask for the recipe. I follow the ingredients exactly. I have found if you make it exactly according to instructions though, the jello layer will seep into the bottom layers and the crust crumbles when cutting. To prevent these issues freeze the curst layer before adding cream cheese layer. Then freeze again with cream cheese layer on. I also allow the jello/strawberry mix to set up nearly all the way before adding to the layers. You will get a perfect, easy to serve layered dessert everytime this way.

This was so easy to make. I followed exactly and I made sure the cream cheese filling completely covered the pretzel crust and no bellow seeped down. Everyone grabbed some saying things like, it’s my favorite, my Mom always made this and it wouldn’t be thanksgiving without this. Thanks!! Enjoy!!
This was a good reminder dish from my family past Christmas Parties. I miss those days ❤️
Love the creme cheese and jello mixtures. However next time, I’ll make with a graham cracker crust.
Delicious! I only used 2 c of pretzels and 3 T of white sugar on the crust but everything else was the same.
Enjoyed by all.
It was a hit at my dinner table for my guests. I shared the recipe!
Could use a little less sugar but this is such a tasty dish!

My daughter maid this pretzel salad the first time I ate it I had 2or 3 paces she left the rest for dad omg I ate all that night. Its crunches and sweet it all taste so wonder full , this is a keeper.

Amazing flavor!! The sweet strawberries with luscious cream cheese filling, combined with the saltiness and crunchiness of the pretzel crust, is an explosion of different tastes that is utterly sublime. YUM! It sounded strange when I first heard of this dessert, and it is extremely different than anything else I have tasted. Which is why I crave this dessert SO much! IT is definitely a crowd-pleaser EVERY TIME!!
